entities.summary:
Kong He, also known as Shuliang He, was a scholar-official and military officer of the State of Lu in ancient China. He served as a prime minister under King Gonggong from 570 to 547 BCE and played a crucial role in the development of Confucianism. Kong He was the son of Bo Xia, a prominent political figure, and the father of Kong Pi and Confucius, who would later become one of the most influential figures in Chinese history. Kong He's legacy extends beyond his own time, as his teachings and ideas would shape the course of Chinese philosophy and governance.

Kong He was born around 600 BCE and died in 547 BCE. He was known for his administrative skills, military prowess, and philosophical insights. Kong He's contributions to Confucianism include his work on the 'Anle Si' (Book of Etiquette), which emphasized the importance of moral character and social hierarchy.

Kong He's significance lies in his role as a unifying force during a period of significant change in ancient China. His leadership and vision helped to stabilize the State of Lu and promote the development of Confucianism, which would go on to shape Chinese philosophy and governance for centuries to come.

Despite his significant contributions, Kong He's life remains somewhat of a mystery. There is limited information available about his early life, and much of what we know about him comes from the accounts of later Confucian scholars.

However, Kong He's legacy is undeniable. His teachings and ideas continue to influence Chinese thought and culture to this day, and his contributions to Confucianism remain an important part of the history of Chinese philosophy.
